text: Working with APIs is a key skill for modern developers. An API lets your program communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests, usually using methods like GET or POST. Most APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can access an API, you often need authentication, such as an API key or token, to prove who you are. Be careful with rate limits, because services restrict how many requests you can make in a certain time. Finally, always add error handling to your code, so your application can respond properly when something goes wrong.
